subject: Proposed Medford Charter Ballot Question
overview: Host John Petrella interviewed Charter Study Committee members Milva McDonald and Ron Giovino to discuss details of the proposed Medford city charter ahead of the November election.

items.title: Introduction and Candidate Invitation
items.summary: Host John Petrella introduced the program and extended an open invitation to candidates running for local office in Medford to appear on the show.

items.title: Introduction of Charter Study Committee Guests
items.summary: Petrella introduced guests Milva McDonald and Ron Giovino to discuss the proposed city charter appearing on the upcoming November ballot.

items.title: Charter Review Timeline
items.summary: Giovino explained that the proposed charter mandates a review every 10 years, with the first review scheduled within five years of implementation.

items.title: City Council Size and Ward Representation
items.summary: McDonald and Giovino discussed expanding the City Council from seven to 11 members, transitioning to a hybrid system of eight ward representatives and three at-large seats.

items.title: Council Appointment Powers
items.summary: McDonald outlined how the proposed charter gives the City Council collaborative involvement in appointing members to local boards and commissions.

items.title: Mayoral Term and Role Adjustments
items.summary: Giovino explained that the mayor's term would increase to four years with a 16-year maximum limit, and the mayor would step down as chairperson of the School Committee.

items.title: School Committee Structural Changes
items.summary: Giovino detailed how the School Committee would adopt a four-district representation model while maintaining its seven-member size.

items.title: Joint Budgeting Meetings
items.summary: McDonald described a new requirement for a joint annual budget meeting between the mayor, City Council, and School Committee on or before February 15.

items.title: Election Ballot Name Placement
items.summary: Giovino noted that the proposed charter introduces a random drawing process for ballot name placement to eliminate advantages for incumbents.

items.title: Citizen Participation Mechanisms
items.summary: McDonald highlighted a new charter section establishing mechanisms for group petitions, ballot initiatives, overturning council decisions, and mayoral recalls.

items.title: Charter Vacancy Provisions and Operating Details
items.summary: McDonald and Giovino discussed draft updates, including new clear vacancy guidelines for leadership and clarifications on the budget-dependent nature of hiring council staff.

items.title: Campaign Resources and Public Outreach
items.summary: The guests shared information about the campaign website and opportunities for residents to obtain lawn signs and campaign literature.

items.title: Program Conclusion
items.summary: Petrella concluded the episode by thanking the guests and inviting residents to connect with the program via email, their website, and YouTube.
